parts.text:
8
A person of mass 60 kg stands on accurate bathroom scales, placed on the floor of an
elevator (lift) which operates in a tall building.
At a certain instant the bathroom scales read 58 kg.
Which row could give the person’s direction of movement and type of motion?
direction
motion
A
downwards
constant speed
B
downwards
slowing down
C
upwards
constant speed
D
upwards
slowing down

hints: Notice the scales read $58\text{ kg}$ while the true mass is $60\text{ kg}$, so the apparent weight and normal force $R$ are smaller than $mg$.
Use $R - mg = ma$ with upward as positive: $R < mg$ means the acceleration $a$ must be negative, i.e. directed downwards.
A downward acceleration can occur in two ways: speeding up downwards or slowing down upwards - check which direction plus slowing or speeding combination matches this.
walkthrough: The scales do not measure mass directly; they measure the normal contact force $R$ pushing up on the person and convert it to a mass reading using $R = m_{apparent}g$.
Here $m_{apparent} = 58\text{ kg}$ is less than the true $60\text{ kg}$, so $R = 58g$ is less than the weight $mg = 60g$.
For vertical motion, Newton's second law gives $R - mg = ma$, taking upwards as positive, so $a = (R-mg)/m$ is negative.
A negative, downward acceleration means the resultant force is downwards. This happens when moving downwards and speeding up, or when moving upwards and slowing down.
Of the listed rows, moving upwards while slowing down gives acceleration downwards and $R < mg$. This is option D.

A.explanation: Constant speed means zero acceleration, so $R = mg$ and the scales would still read $60\text{ kg}$, not $58\text{ kg}$.

B.explanation: Slowing down while moving downwards needs upward acceleration, so $R > mg$ and the reading would be greater than $60\text{ kg}$.

C.explanation: Constant speed upwards also has zero acceleration, so the normal contact force equals weight and the reading stays at $60\text{ kg}$.

D.explanation: Slowing down while moving upwards needs downward acceleration, so $R < mg$ and the $58\text{ kg}$ reading is less than the true $60\text{ kg}$.
